correctness.rationale: The cut x(H)<=k-1 removes the one forbidden vertex without new edge intersections because hypersimplex edges exchange one 0 and one 1. Reflection containment is equivalent to coordinate constraints 1<=z_i<=s, total z([n])=k(s+1), plus one exact cut bound z(H)<=s(k-1)+max(0,k-l). Summing establishes four sharp lower bounds; equality constraints yield one unique uniform center at rank-corank gap>=2, a unique nonuniform center at equal rank and corank, or a full simplex of dimension min(k,l) at gap one. The four cases include every center and all integer boundaries. The standalone verifier checks 36 profiles, 48,164 vertices, and 212,798 exact rational reflected-vertex instances; independent full linear programs checked 64 profiles. Experiments are explicitly corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The claim concerns arbitrary ranks and coranks at least three, exact rank--corank asymmetry loss, and all minimizer centers for deleting exactly one basis of a uniform matroid. Inspected primary matroid articles address polyhedral reconstruction, circuit-hyperplane Ehrhart splits, and valuations, not this center law. The general robust-center LP does not state its explicit closed form or contact regimes. The accessible full mathematical rank-two classification and complement duality apply only when the rank or corank is two; the present domain explicitly excludes both. Searches of published mathematical records and primary literature did not identify a theorem implying this new complete classification; plausible older equivalent terminology remains a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Historical formulations under alternative names (Minkowski measure of symmetry, deleted-basis sparse paving matroids, hyperplane splits) may escape the indexed searches.
The general computational optimization literature might contain isolated tabulated instances, but no stronger all-integer theorem was found in inspected material.
Independent bibliographic priority assessment remains unperformed.

value.rationale: A one-basis deletion of the uniform-matroid polytope is a canonical minimal combinatorial perturbation. The asymmetry suffers an exactly quantified loss only at ranks differing from coranks by at most one. Surprisingly, gap one creates a positive-dimensional simplex of all optimal centers rather than a unique minimizer, of dimension arbitrarily large while a balanced example remains uniquely centered. This sharp stability and center-locus phase diagram for all rank and corank at least three is meaningful beyond generic robust LP feasibility and standard Ehrhart-split facts.
